# Phase V1 -- SIGEL 1.3's own load-and-save round trip, captured 2026-08-27 on
# the x86 box through the sigel-x86 session. 1.3 is frozen, so this never
# changes and never needs recapturing.
#
# METHOD (theirs): copies in a scratch directory, one per experiment; pristine
# downloads verified unchanged by md5 afterwards. No pvmd was running, so every
# pvm_addhosts failed and no slave was ever spawned -- load, save, quit, with
# evaluation impossible rather than merely disabled. Zero generations in all
# four runs. Repointing the dead 2003 paths necessarily edits a Body line
# INSIDE the block being compared, so they diffed edited-input against output
# rather than pristine against output.
#
# IN  = the order the shipped .exp stores.
# OUT = the order 1.3 wrote back, i.e. Qt 2's QDict iteration order over IN.
#
# OUT is the line that matters: it is what our Q2Dict had to reproduce.

== twoBasesSimpleFitness1.exp   ROBOT BLOCK IDENTICAL (2 links, 1 joint: nothing collides)
# The command list permuted even here -- that dict holds 13 entries whatever
# the robot's size, so "twoBases is the control" scopes to the robot
# containers, not to LanguageParameters.

== octopusSimpleFitness.exp
material IN =OUT: greenPlastic bluePlastic redPlastic
link     IN =OUT: thirdFootLink firstFootLink base firstLegLink1 firstLegLink2 secondFootLink secondLegLink1 secondLegLink2 thirdLegLink1 thirdLegLink2
joint    IN : secondLegJoint1 thirdLegJoint1 secondLegJoint2 thirdLegJoint2 secondLegJoint3 thirdLegJoint3 firstLegJoint1 firstLegJoint2 firstLegJoint3
joint    OUT: secondLegJoint1 secondLegJoint2 thirdLegJoint1 secondLegJoint3 thirdLegJoint2 thirdLegJoint3 firstLegJoint1 firstLegJoint2 firstLegJoint3
drive    IN : firstLegJoint2Drive firstLegJoint1Drive secondLegJoint1Drive thirdLegJoint2Drive secondLegJoint3Drive thirdLegJoint3Drive secondLegJoint2Drive thirdLegJoint1Drive firstLegJoint3Drive
drive    OUT: firstLegJoint2Drive firstLegJoint1Drive secondLegJoint1Drive secondLegJoint3Drive thirdLegJoint2Drive secondLegJoint2Drive thirdLegJoint3Drive thirdLegJoint1Drive firstLegJoint3Drive
sensor   IN : thirdLegJoint3Sensor secondLegJoint1Sensor secondLegJoint2Sensor firstLegJoint3Sensor thirdLegJoint2Sensor secondLegJoint3Sensor thirdLegJoint1Sensor firstLegJoint1Sensor firstLegJoint2Sensor
sensor   OUT: secondLegJoint1Sensor thirdLegJoint3Sensor secondLegJoint2Sensor firstLegJoint3Sensor secondLegJoint3Sensor thirdLegJoint2Sensor thirdLegJoint1Sensor firstLegJoint1Sensor firstLegJoint2Sensor
body     OUT: legLink.wrl footLink.wrl tripleBase.wrl        (IN: footLink, legLink, tripleBase)

== walkerNiceWalkingFitness.exp
material IN : footMaterial legMaterial bodyMaterial shoulderMaterial

points   walker leg1 IN : leg1PredNormal leg1SuccNormal leg1SuccBase leg1SuccDir leg1PredDir leg1PredBase
points   walker leg1 OUT: leg1PredNormal leg1SuccBase leg1SuccNormal leg1SuccDir leg1PredBase leg1PredDir

# THE ROUND TRIP IS AN INVOLUTION. The command list toggles between exactly two
# orders and nothing else:
#   A = MUL MOVE CMP COPY LOAD SENSE SUB DIV MIN DELAY ADD MOD MAX
#   B = MUL CMP MOVE COPY LOAD SENSE DIV SUB ADD DELAY MIN MAX MOD
# twoBases A->B, octopusNice A->B, octopusSimple B->A, walker B->A. The two
# octopus files are the same robot shipped in opposite orders -- each one's
# input is the other's output, across every container. Applying the transform
# twice returns the original, which is what bucket reversal on prepend
# predicts, so this is positive evidence for the model rather than mere
# consistency with it.

RESULT 2026-09-18 -- all 14 shipped .exp, and the robot a 1.3 slave receives

# with \n, no trailing newline.

pass a fresh load of the previous output.

--- THE ROBOT A 1.3 SLAVE RECEIVES, verbatim ---
Captured on the MASTER at the send: SIG_GPFitnessTrainer::spawnTask ->
SIG_GPPVMData::savePVMDataTransfer (writes, precision 50) ->
SIG_GPPVMData::sendQStringToPVM (pvm_initsend / pvm_pkint / pvm_pkstr / pvm_send).
MEASURED at pvm_send: msgtag=23. Fitness comes back through pvm_upkdouble, a raw
double; the master never calls pvm_upkstr.
Per experiment, before the run: the dead 2003 roots substituted to the run dir,
all PVMHOST entries collapsed to one local host, termination moved to 2030 and one
generation, FITNESS of POOLPOS 0,1,2 set to -1. Robot block untouched.

# "Axis groups permute INSIDE a single Link line, in 6 of 14": the list names 7 --
#   hammer, insect, both octopus, both runner, walker. The ff6db93 baseline gives 7

# oracle's reconciliation, verbatim: "2 ties in pass-through data -- both in line 2,
# tokens 17 and 20, the 1.11667 pair. These are the only float tokens whose doubles
# are identical on both sides, so these are the only ties that MUST appear on yours
# too. 18 ties in computed data ... whether a given token lands exactly on a tie is a
# property of each side's own value."

--- THE JOINT ORDER A 1.3 SLAVE GETS AFTER A FRESH .rrb IMPORT, 1.3, verbatim ---
Predictions written by the oracle before the run:
  P6. The tag-23 payload's RotationalJoint order will be flip(H) (H = the order a save
      of the fresh import writes = the shipped octopusSimpleFitness order).
  P7. The joint walk still starts at secondLegJoint1 for base.
  P8. The saved-and-reloaded control will give H, not flip(H).
FRESH case, no save, no reload. GUI: File > New Experiment, Import > Robot (octopus.rrb),
Import > GP-Parameters (a .gpp carrying PVMHOST, FITNESSNAME SimpleFitnessFunction and
the termination keys), Individuals > Add 10, then gdb attached to the master and armed
BEFORE Start, breaking at pvm_pkstr/pvm_send. 16 tag-23 payloads, ONE distinct joint order.
CONTROL: the same robot saved (the Q4 import) then loaded from disk, GP-Parameters
imported, 10 individuals added, Start. 16 payloads, one distinct order. The saved file's
container order is byte-for-byte the shipped octopusSimpleFitness order.
  A  fresh import, payload joints
     secondLegJoint1(3), secondLegJoint2(4), thirdLegJoint1(6), secondLegJoint3(5),
     thirdLegJoint2(7), thirdLegJoint3(8), firstLegJoint1(0), firstLegJoint2(1), firstLegJoint3(2)
  B  the saved file's OWN order H (what Q4 emitted, = shipped order)
     secondLegJoint1(3), thirdLegJoint1(6), secondLegJoint2(4), thirdLegJoint2(7),
     secondLegJoint3(5), thirdLegJoint3(8), firstLegJoint1(0), firstLegJoint2(1), firstLegJoint3(2)
  C  that saved file reloaded, payload joints -- equals B exactly.
  P6  fresh payload == flip(H)   TRUE   (A is the Q2 pass-1 order)
  P7  base's first joint is secondLegJoint1 in BOTH   TRUE
  P8  reloaded payload == H, and fresh != reloaded   TRUE
Which entity kinds move between A and C:
    Body             DIFFER   legLink,footLink,tripleBase   vs  footLink,legLink,tripleBase
    RotationalJoint  DIFFER
    Drive            DIFFER
    JointSensor      DIFFER
    Material         IDENTICAL
    Link             IDENTICAL
Numbers are unchanged throughout: every entity carries its .rrb declaration index in both.
THE RULE: payload order = flip(what a save from that same state would write). It
alternates with every save.

--- OURS, for the same robot ---
# Base's joints in the order each .rrb declares them:
#   data/octopus/octopus.rrb (as shipped)   firstLegJoint1, secondLegJoint1, thirdLegJoint1
#   data-reordered/octopus/octopus.rrb      secondLegJoint1, thirdLegJoint1, firstLegJoint1
# The reordered file declares all nine joints in exactly order H. In both A and H,
# base's three joints come second leg, third leg, first leg.
